name: Houston
lede: Big, flat, and full of distance holes — Houston's disc golf runs from open river parks to wooded church campuses. We're publishing the metro's best first.
introParagraphs: Houston disc golf is bigger than it looks on a map. T.C. Jester is the city's friendly 21-hole classic with distance holes and a blue-tee layout past 8,300 feet, while Texas Army Trail in Cypress and Agnes Moffitt's flat, tree-lined 21 holes round out the open-side of the scene.

Northside Christian in Spring is the hidden heavyweight — a church-campus course with USDGC-style par 4s, tight woods, and four water hazards. The Houston Disc Golf community runs Sunday Funday events and Zube Tuesday leagues, and nearly all of Houston's mapped courses are free to play. Summer heat is the main challenge — play early or late.
New here? Agnes Moffitt is the friendliest intro; Northside is the test. For gear, The Spring Country Club is the local disc golf store.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Houston metro?
faqs.answer: There are 84 courses across the Houston metro, mapped and live on FindFrolf, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Houston?
faqs.answer: Texas Army Trail in Cypress and Northside Christian in Spring top the published list — one a long open test, the other a wooded championship challenge.

faqs.question: Are Houston's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Most are. 83 of the 84 mapped courses are free to play, and 1 is pay-to-play. Check each course page for its current green fee.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Houston?
faqs.answer: Agnes Moffitt — flat, tree-lined, and friendly from the red tees. T.C. Jester is another accessible option with plenty of room.

faqs.question: Where can I buy disc golf gear in Houston?
faqs.answer: The Spring Country Club is the local disc golf store. Play It Again Sports in Houston carries new and used discs and starter sets.
